transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Asteria - Security), Maya Chen (Asteria - CTO), Diego Alvarez (Asteria - Platform)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on whether Asteria can use Redwood Hosted for their PII-sensitive inference workloads vs Dedicated/Private deployment. Key topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention and egress controls.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving time. I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Samira our SE. We're here to run through your security bar and answer questions on hosted vs dedicated vs private. Jordan, Maya, Diego, you want to intro briefly?
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Yeah, sure. Jordan here, Security Manager at Asteria. We're a mid-size biotech, handling de-identified patient data but still, uh, fairly strict compliance.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Maya, CTO. We're evaluating LLM inference to power internal triage and some customer-facing summarization, so latency and data controls matter.
[00:39] Diego Alvarez: Diego, platform. I'll be working with infra if we go Dedicated or Private.
[00:44] Samira Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), identity and access (SSO/SAML, RBAC), telemetry/audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention controls. Then Q&A and next steps.

[01:05] Jordan Lee: Top-level question: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? And are those available for customers to review?
[01:15] Alex Kim: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and we also have an ISO 27001 summary. We'll share the certs and the standard report; full reports require an NDA in some cases but we'll provide everything you need. Link to docs: https://redwood.ai/security (note: auto transcript might show red wood or red wood dedicated sometimes).

[01:40] Maya Chen: For hosted, our legal and security teams are sensitive about keys and data retention. If a request includes PHI-derived text even if de-identified, we need to control retention and encryption at rest. What's Redwood's approach?
[01:55] Samira Patel: On Hosted we offer customer data encryption at rest, and service-side encryption keys managed by Redwood by default. For stricter control we support customer-managed keys (KMS) on Dedicated/Private via bring-your-own-KMS options \u2014 HSM integrations are possible for Private.

[02:20] Diego Alvarez: So for Hosted with BYOK is that available? I thought BYOK required Dedicated.
[02:25] Alex Kim: Good question \u2014 BYOK is typically part of our Dedicated and Private tiers. On hosted we have envelope encryption and strong access controls but the master KMS is Redwood-managed. For customers requiring FIPS-level key control or HSM-backed KMS, we recommend Dedicated or Private.

[02:45] Jordan Lee: Audit logs \u2014 we need immutable audit trails for every model invocation and config change, available for at least 3 years for our auditors. What granularity and retention?
[03:00] Samira Patel: We capture request-level metadata (timestamp, request id, model version, user id, route), and admin activity (who deployed, who changed ACLs). Hosted includes 90 days by default, extended retention is an add-on. Dedicated and Private give you full control \u2014 logs can be exported to your Splunk/Datadog/S3 and retained as your policy requires. We can support three years on Dedicated/Private or via our add-on for hosted.

[03:30] Maya Chen: RBAC \u2014 do you integrate with our IdP? We use Okta and SAML 2.0. Need SCIM for provisioning.
[03:40] Alex Kim: Yes, SSO via SAML is supported across Hosted and Dedicated, SCIM provisioning is available. For Private deployments you control IdP integration directly. Roles can be mapped to groups and we support fine-grained RBAC for route-level and model-level permissions.

[04:00] Jordan Lee: What about service-to-service auth? We want short-lived tokens, least privilege.
[04:08] Samira Patel: We issue scoped API keys and support short-lived tokens and OAuth flows for service accounts. For Dedicated/Private we can wire in your internal token service; for Hosted we have token rotation and scoped keys.

[04:28] Diego Alvarez: Network controls \u2014 can we restrict egress and have VPC peering?
[04:35] Alex Kim: Dedicated supports private networking and VPC peering. Private gives you an on-prem or VPC deployment entirely behind your network boundary. Hosted has IP allowlisting and private connectivity options in select regions.

[04:50] Jordan Lee: Data residency \u2014 we need data never to leave EU for EU customers. Is that enforced?
[04:57] Samira Patel: Yes, regional deployments and routing ensure data stays in the chosen region. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private to guarantee it.

[05:12] Maya Chen: A bit about model behavior \u2014 do you cache prompts or maintain KV cache logs that could leak context? We run clinical prompts that must not be re-used.
[05:23] Samira Patel: The runtime uses KV cache to speed inference, but we have strict isolation per-tenant. For Hosted we have prefix caching options and you can opt out of persistent prefix caching. Dedicated/Private gives you full control to disable caching or configure retention windows.

[05:45] Jordan Lee: Encryption in transit? TLS? Mutual TLS?
[05:48] Alex Kim: All traffic is TLS 1.2+; mTLS is available for Private and can be configured for Dedicated. Hosted supports standard TLS and client certs in some setups.

[06:00] Diego Alvarez: How about redwood's internal access controls \u2014 who at Redwood can access customer data or logs? Need explanation for SOC2 audit.

[06:10] Alex Kim: We have least-privilege internal access, audited SRE and ops roles, and break-glass controls. Access requires 2FA and is logged \u2014 these procedures are in the SOC2 report. We'll highlight those sections when we share the report.

[06:30] Maya Chen: Any external pen tests or vuln scans we can review?
[06:34] Samira Patel: We do regular third-party assessments and vulnerability scanning; executive summaries are fine to share, and we can coordinate redacted reports under NDA.

[06:50] Jordan Lee: About retention: we need a data retention matrix\u2014how long do you keep request logs, payloads, model outputs, and are there deletion APIs?
[07:02] Samira Patel: By default hosted request payloads and short-term logs are kept for 90 days. We provide deletion APIs and can do on-demand deletions for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we also offer a retention customization add-on. We'll send the retention matrix.

[07:25] Diego Alvarez: Is there a way to scrub PII before it hits Redwood? We might want an agent that redacts certain fields client-side.
[07:33] Alex Kim: Yes \u2014 common pattern is client-side pre-processing and tokenization. We also support field-level redaction, but that's implemented by the customer or via a preprocessing lambda in Dedicated/Private patterns. We can help with a reference scrubber script.

[07:50] Jordan Lee: Ok, so likely path: initial hosted trial with reduced retention + encryption, evaluate performance, then move to Dedicated if we need BYOK/HSM and full log export.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Timeline: we want to be piloting in 6\u20138 weeks if possible.

[08:05] Samira Patel: That's reasonable. For the pilot we'll propose a sandbox tenant with limited retention, and a small Dedicated benchmark if you want BYOK tests.

[08:18] Alex Kim: Competitors \u2014 we hear you might be evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI, and also considering Oracle's managed offerings. Differences: Redwood aims to give more control over serving (dedicated pools, BYOK, private control plane) and transparent performance/observability.

[08:40] Jordan Lee: A few nitty-gritty questions: do you support log signing / tamper-evident logs for audits?
[08:47] Samira Patel: We have append-only logs and can export to your log store; for tamper-evident chain signing we can integrate tools like AWS CloudTrail + S3 object locking or third-party WORM storage in Dedicated/Private setups.

[09:05] Diego Alvarez: What about model version pinning and rollback auditing?
[09:10] Alex Kim: You can pin model versions per route, we version everything and have deployment audit events. Rollbacks are recorded and visible in the console and in the activity logs.

[09:25] Maya Chen: Any SLA for data deletion when requested? Our legal wants commitments.
[09:30] Samira Patel: For Dedicated/Private we can contractually commit deletion windows. For Hosted we offer contractual SLAs for deletion as part of an enterprise add-on \u2014 we'll surface exact language in the DPA and security docs.

[09:50] Jordan Lee: On the ops side, incident response \u2014 do you notify customers on incidents affecting confidentiality?
[09:57] Alex Kim: Yes, we have incident response processes, we notify impacted customers within our SLA windows, and we provide post-incident reports. These are summarized in the security pack we'll send.

[10:15] Samira Patel: Quick technical note on benchmarking: for latency-sensitive use cases we suggest a small benchmark of your typical prompt shapes and sequence lengths. We'll run tests on our dedicated pool to show p95/p99 latencies per model.

[10:34] Jordan Lee: For compliance we'll likely need the SOC2 report, ISO summary, pen test summary, and a DPA.

[10:41] Alex Kim: Agreed \u2014 we'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, an exec-level pen test summary, and our DPA template. I'll include contact for legal to sync.

[11:00] Maya Chen: A couple more questions about multi-tenant isolation on hosted \u2014 are model weights ever shared across tenants? Could there be cross-tenant cache leaks?
[11:10] Samira Patel: No model weights are shared; runtime enforces tenant isolation. The KV cache is namespaced per tenant and we do not share cached contexts across tenants. For extra assurance you can opt out of persistent caches on Hosted.

[11:30] Jordan Lee: Is there a formal change management / release calendar we can review?
[11:35] Alex Kim: Yes, we publish release notes and have scheduled maintenance windows; enterprise customers get advance notice and a maintenance calendar. We'll share the calendar link.

[11:50] Diego Alvarez: Anything about data provenance? We need to track which data used to fine-tune models if that comes up.
[11:58] Samira Patel: We don't currently support customer-side fine-tuning on hosted in a way that mixes data; for Dedicated/Private you can manage your fine-tune artifacts and provenance in your storage. We'll add notes on provenance and model lineage for the docs we share.

[12:20] Alex Kim: Alright quick recap \u2014 we'll send SOC2, ISO, pen test summ, retention matrix, DPA, and an architecture diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options. Samira will set up the sandbox and benchmark plan. Jordan will share retention policy and IdP details.

[12:40] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Two small asks: 1) can you redact example payloads in the SOC2 docs? 2) Include a sample SCIM group-to-role mapping?
[12:50] Alex Kim: Yep on both \u2014 we'll prepare sanitized examples and a SCIM mapping sample.

[13:00] Maya Chen: Thanks \u2014 we'll review and pick a path.

[13:05] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the package and schedule the SE deep-dive.

[13:12] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "red wood" vs "Redwood"), speaker overlap at times, and some shorthand.
